To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) HM contamination significantly affected AMF growth and their related GRSP production, and subsequently influenced aggregate distribution and stability in HM polluted soils; (2) the introduction of plant associated with AMFs could be an effective biotechnological approach for improving soil aggregate stability and ecosystem functioning in HM contaminated area.

the effects of heavy metals (HMs) on glomalin related soil protein (GRPS) and soil aggregate formation and stability in HM polluted soil were dependent on soil depth and that GRSP played an important role in soil aggregate formation and stabilization.
the HM contamination inhibited the AMF growth and GRSP production, and the GRSP accumulation was significantly correlated with soil properties and aggregate stability in HM polluted soils.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ecological functions of AMF-GRSP in HM polluted soils, which could be used as a reference to further study the mechanisms of AMF in the restoration of HM polluted soils.
the potential role of GRSP in improving aggregate formation and stability, and the importance of plant-AMF association for ecological restoration in HM contaminated soils.
the potential role of AMF in soil organic matter accumulation and aggregate formation, which will be beneficial for understanding soil processes and ecosystem restoration in HM polluted soils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

GRSP is a key indicator of AMF growth and its relationship with soil properties, and GRSP and AMF could be considered as the potential biomarker for HM pollution assessment and ecological restoration in HM polluted soils.
the effects of HM contamination on soil properties, AMF growth and aggregate distribution and stability are significantly influenced by soil depths.

the HM contamination significantly inhibited AMF status and GRSP production, and that GRSP accumulation was significantly correlated with soil properties and aggregate formation, which was essential for soil aggregate stability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AMF-plant symbiosis could be an important tool in ecological restoration, especially for soils contaminated by Pb and Zn.
the introduction of AMF into the contaminated soils could be a successful biotechnology tool to assist the ecological restoration of HM-polluted soils.

the introduction of AMF can improve the soil aggregate stability by increasing the content of GRSP and SOM, which could be used as a potential bioindicator of AMF colonization and a useful tool for the evaluation of soil restoration in HM polluted area.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the application of AMF in the remediation of contaminated soil should consider the depth of soil contamination and the effects of HM on AMF growth.
the application of AMF in ecological restoration should be based on the soil depth and type of heavy metal pollution.
the GRSP is a key factor for soil aggregation and aggregate stability, which can be affected by AMF, soil properties and HM contamination.
